sections.title: Put fine art next to Monet — then turn QT off
sections.lede: Classical painters need the genre word. Booru tags and Quality Tags fight them. Staff said it out loud.
sections.body:
ght901 (Anlatan Team / Web Dev) drew a clean line on classical painters this window: put `fine art` beside the artist tag, or the model leans anime. Booru-style tags and the Quality Tags preset both pull hard toward the anime prior, so Monet (and friends) get watered down into soft pastel fanart unless you name the genre. The staff demos were blunt — `fine art, artist:claude monet, flowers` and the character-adjacent `1girl, fine art, artist:claude monet, flowers,`. Characters under fine art may not look how you want; that is the trade. Room echo still counts as ANECDOTE: Quality Tags = strong anime bias, and missing `fine art` got called out in the Monet threads. Public stills on this sheet are flitter's landscape progression and the 5× Monet-without-fine-art tile — the youthful staff character Monet still stays off the board.

**Try this.** Same seed, two gens, V5 Full, Euler / karras, guidance 5–6, 23–28 steps, QT **off**, rescale 0. A: `fine art, artist:claude monet, flowers, garden path, soft daylight`. B: drop `fine art` and leave everything else identical. Look for brushy impressionist light vs anime-clean petals. If A reads painterly and B slides cute, save_memory the pair.

**Why it matters.** Classical artist tags without the genre word are fighting QT. Test it once this weekend before you blame the artist alias.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: In general for those kind of artists you should include `fine art` in the prompt, but prompting booru tags and such will also inevitably weaken them. You also might not like how characters tend to look with fine art though. The prompt for that one was just `fine art, artist:claude monet, flowers`

sections.title: Collapse the wardrobe, then turn CFG down
sections.lede: Name the clothes. Raise confidence. Variation comes back when you lower the guidance — sometimes to zero.
sections.body:
.mahouko (AI Developer) restated a core prompting principle this week: do not stop at the character name. Write everything you know about clothing and appearance so the distribution collapses and the model's confidence goes up. DanTagGen-style expansion does the same job — more known facts, less guessing. Once the prompt is dense enough, you get variation back by **reducing CFG**, not by deleting detail. Clear enough prompts can look good without CFG at all; ambiguous dataset labels still need CFG for prompt-relevance. That is staff language, not a community vibes essay. If your character keeps drifting outfits between seeds, you under-specified the wardrobe. If the wardrobe is locked and the face feels frozen, your guidance is too high for the confidence you already bought.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler / karras, QT on, rescale 0, 23 steps. Gen A — character name only: `1girl, asuna yuuki, standing, looking at viewer`. Gen B — collapse: `1girl, asuna yuuki, long orange hair, blue eyes, white shirt, dark skirt, red ribbon, standing, looking at viewer`. Run B again at guidance 7, then 4, then 0. Watch outfit lock at high CFG, then soft variation as CFG falls. If B@0 still holds identity better than A@7, the collapse worked.

**Call to action.** Pick one character you always under-prompt. Collapse once. Ladder CFG. Same-seed compare. Save the rung that still looks alive.

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: usually what I do with prompting is: I don't stop at just the character name, I write everything I know about their clothing and appearance, to collapse the distribution and increase the model's confidence

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: to get the variation back you reduce CFG

excerpts.speaker: .mahouko
excerpts.text: you can get nice images without CFG if your prompt is clear enough

sections.title: Don't pepper the mask
sections.lede: Inpaint only alters near the hole. A spray of nearby patches slowly eats the image.
sections.body:
ght901's inpaint hygiene note is short and worth framing on the wall: the edit stays local to the mask; repeated inpaints on the same general area slowly deteriorate the image; do not inpaint a bunch of small regions in close proximity. Keep masks sparse. Pair that with earlier staff language that inpaint in-context learning is strong — the model can borrow from what it can see — but hygiene still matters. Peppering five tiny holes around an eye will look fine for two passes and muddy by pass six. One clean mask that covers the whole problem region beats a constellation of micro-edits. If you need multi-region work, leave breathing room between patches, or finish one area before opening another.

**Try this.** Take a keeper you like. V5 Full inpaint, Euler, guidance ~5, QT on, rescale 0. Bad path: three tiny masks within a thumb's width of each other (eye, cheek, lip) and regen each. Good path: one connected mask covering the whole face region once. Same seed where the UI allows. Look for progressive mush and halo on the peppered path versus a single coherent rewrite on the sparse path.

**Why it matters.** Inpaint is not free undo. Every nearby patch taxes the pixels you already liked. Sparse first.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: It should only alter the area just around where you inpaint. If you do repeated inpaints targeting the same general area the image is going to slowly deteriorate over time

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: In general I wouldn't recommend inpainting a bunch of small areas in close proximity.

sections.title: The pink ladder, and why 0:: still matters
sections.lede: Bare `pink` in UC is not the same as `0::pink::`. The middle rung is `0.2::`.
sections.body:
0hdot posted a three-rung UC color comparison that should live next to every 0:: teaching slide: add `pink` to UC, then `0.2::pink::`, then `0::pink::`, and look at the stills. Bare tag negation, soft weight, and zero-weight are three different tools. This reinforces the existing HOUSE/guide story about 0:: versus true negation — do **not** re-promote the ladder as brand-new CONSENSUS. It is digest reinforcement with a public board image. If you have been dumping color words into UC and wondering why the palette barely moves, you may be on the wrong rung. Same seed across the three UC strings is the only honest read.

**Try this.** V5 Full, Euler / karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Prompt: `1girl, white dress, outdoor cafe, soft daylight` (no pink in the prompt). Same seed three times — UC A: `pink`. UC B: `0.2::pink::`. UC C: `0::pink::`. Look for how aggressively pink accents vanish or soften. If pixels agree with 0hdot's board, save_memory the ladder.

**Call to action.** One color you keep fighting. Three UC rungs. Same seed. Pick the rung that actually moves the palette.

**Try this.** Open Explore. Filter to V5 + your preferred aspect + VT on (or off). Compare three keepers that match your next job. Steal the workflow, not the prompt dump.

**Call to action.** Five minutes. Filter Explore before you invent a new stack.

sections.body:
matts7123 on unofficial nai-image-gen-discussion: Transparent BG injects tags that bias toward large negative space. You can fight with UC or weighted negative space in the main prompt, but turning the toggle off is simpler. Keep **[UNOFFICIAL]** until echoed on official. UI screenshot stays on the grim board only — not the public billboard.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Prompt: `1girl, standing, city street, crowd behind`. Gen A: Transparent BG **off**. Gen B: Transparent BG **on**. Look for sudden empty fields / subject floating in white. If B opens a crater of negative space, leave the toggle off for scene work.

**Why it matters.** Do not burn Opus fighting a toggle with UC when the switch is right there.

excerpts.speaker: matts7123
excerpts.text: If transparent BG is on (checked) it will add tags in the background that push the model into adding large amounts of negative space to your gens.  you can add negative space to UC or in the main prompt with large negative strength, but it's easier to turn transparent BG off.

sections.lede: Checked on → background tags push large empty space. Easier to turn off than to UC-fight it.
sections.title: Transparent BG is a negative-space injector

sections.body:
**Finish tags are not all photoreal.** Anime faces break on `realistic` / Expert Shading panel / photorealism / hyperrealism / unasked `3d` / `detailed face` / `detailed skin` stacks. Prefer Quality or `high complexity` for anime finish. Painted, photo, and 3d jobs may keep those words. Read compiled_prompt when the panel leaks `1.4::realistic::`. Not CONSENSUS.

**MCP `generate_image` ignores character boxes.** Identity and body must live in the base prompt on that path. Studio `apply_studio_changes` still uses boxes — keep identity there. Mixing the two paths is how characters evaporate. Not staff.

**ebiblue-scoped hips.** One isolated box group `2.2–2.8::huge wide hips::` under `artist:ebiblue` can move them. Cap ~2.8. Ban ported V4.5 3–4 stacks. One size word per axis. No new hip/WG/pregnancy recipes in this window. Do not promote to CONSENSUS.

**`semi-anthro torso` is a human-trunk tag.** Never bare `semi-anthro`. Do not UC the torso word. UC `fur, muzzle, snout, tail, paws, digitigrade, animal legs`. Drop `long torso` from the prompt; put it in UC.

Soft reminder from staff this window (zine-only): default QT/UC can lean a bit goopy — not severe. Pair with the QT-stack article above.

sections.body:
sergalaluminum caught a familiar self-own: someone stacked a heavy `2::best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres, ultra detailed, masterpiece, high definition render::` block on top of the Quality Tags preset. The answer was blunt — you are overdoing it and it is having a negative effect; the `very aesthetic, masterpiece` QT already added is enough. This is ANECDOTE leaning soft-tip, not STAFF law, but it matches how QT is supposed to work. Double-stacking quality words is how you get goopy finish and dead eyes while thinking you are "more aesthetic." Soft staff note in the same window: default QT/UC can lean a bit goopy — ght901 does not find it severe — which is another reason not to pile weights on the pile.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler / karras, guidance 5, 23 steps, rescale 0. Gen A: QT **on**, no extra quality block. Gen B: QT on plus `2::best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres, ultra detailed, masterpiece::` in the prompt. Look for plastic skin, overcooked contrast, or lost fine detail on B. If A wins, delete the stack from your templates.

**Why it matters.** QT is a preset, not a suggestion to re-type. Stop paying twice for the same words.

excerpts.speaker: sergalaluminum
excerpts.text:
no, you're overdoing it and it's having a negative effect on your outputs
just the `very aesthetic, masterpiece` that was already added by the quality tags preset is enough to make your images all pretty and whatnot

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: Default QT/UC can lean a bit goopy at times. I don't find it particularly severe though

sections.lede: Quality Tags already injects `very aesthetic, masterpiece`. Piling `2::best quality...::` on top can hurt.
sections.title: Don't double-stack quality on QT

sections.body:
uchariko's advice-channel note is the casing rule that keeps biting people: avoid lowercase `text:` because it changes how the encoder processes what follows. Prefer prose like `the speech bubble says ||"Text1"|"Text2"|"Text3"||`, or keep the capital-T `Text:` form when you need the dedicated syntax. uragan_2024 posted a clean randomizer pairing the spoken line with matching `Text:` inside the same `||...||` block so the bubble and the rendered glyphs stay aligned. Soft pitfalls from the same window (still ANECDOTE): putting the bubble in a character box can point it correctly — or leak/multiply characters if you treat the box as a bubble container. Inpaint remains a fallback when older models choke. HOUSE casing rule still applies: prompt/UC/boxes stay lowercase except `Text:` and quoted sign text.

**Try this.** V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Prompt: `1girl, open mouth, upper body, plain background. speech bubble with text that says ||"hey there". Text: hey there|"what's up?". Text: what's up?||`. Generate a few — confirm the bubble text matches a randomizer arm. Then try the bad casing once: replace with lowercase `text:` and see if the encoder behavior shifts.

**Call to action.** One dialogue line. Capital `Text:`. Randomizer optional. Do not lowercase the keyword.

excerpts.speaker: uchariko
excerpts.text: I can't remember if the `Text:` syntax is case-sensitive, but I would avoid using `text:` anyway, since it changes the way the encoder processes the succeeding terms. Just say `The speech bubble says ||"Text1"|"Text2|"Text3"||` or some variation of that

excerpts.speaker: uragan_2024
excerpts.text:
For a randomizer, my method is this:
`girl, open mouth. Speech bubble with text that says ||"hey there". Text: hey there|"what's up?". Text: what's up?||`

sections.lede: Avoid lowercase `text:`. Prefer prose. Pair the bubble string with `Text:` inside `||...||` if you randomize.
sections.title: Speech bubbles: Text: casing and the randomizer

sections.body:
paragonofmankind chased a copyright-style prompt (`dragon ball (classic)`) that suddenly collapsed into generic AI anime after they added more character tags. Clearing UC while keeping the new characters restored the DB look. The smoking gun in their follow-up: leftover specific characters from **another franchise** sitting in UC from earlier gens. Same character, slightly different tag sets — one version went generic, the other held style — until those foreign UC names were removed, and both versions snapped back. This is ANECDOTE, one user's weekend detective work, not CONSENSUS. But the hygiene lesson is cheap: UC is not a scrap drawer. Franchise leftovers act like silent style vetoes.

**Try this.** Grab a copyright/style prompt that usually works. Same seed, V5 Full, Euler, guidance 5, 23 steps, QT on, rescale 0. Gen A: clean UC (no other-franchise character names). Gen B: add two character names from a different franchise into UC only. Compare style lock. If B goes generic, you just reproduced the anecdote — clear your UC template.

**Why it matters.** Before you rewrite the whole prompt, audit UC for yesterday's cast.

excerpts.speaker: paragonofmankind
excerpts.text:
I am confused. I feel like it didn't use to be like this, but I use an art style using the "copyright" tag (maybe that the wrong way to do it) and it works relatively well, it gives me the style.
Then after adding some more character tags to get what I want, all I get is the most generic of AI gen anime styles and I simply can't get back to the style I had at first. (Tried with dragon ball (classic) )

excerpts.speaker: paragonofmankind
excerpts.text:
I had specific characters from another franchise in the UC from earlier gens. For basically the same character with slightly varying tags (2 versions) it produced different outcomes; one veering towards the generic AI style, the other the prompted DB style.
After removing said specific characters from the UC, I now get the DB style for both versions.

sections.lede: Stale other-franchise names in UC pushed a `dragon ball (classic)` style run into generic anime — until the UC was cleared.
sections.title: Leftover UC characters can kill copyright style

sections.body:
hams0475_90026 described a comic inpaint trick that pairs cleanly with staff "in-context learning" language without becoming CONSENSUS itself: when several characters are on the page and you are inpainting one region, the model gets confused about who to insert. Fix — look at the **unmasked** cast, randomly assign them names, then use those names as precise indications of who belongs in the inpaint region. Same poster on 2-koma: if the character already exists in the top panel, inpaint the bottom panel and let in-context learning copy them — not 100%, but strong. Method is user ANECDOTE; the staff claim it aligns with is "inpaint sees context." Do not invent pleasebankai/triplis low-step board URLs here — those stills are not on this issue's Yozora srcs.

**Try this.** Build or crop a simple 2-panel comic. V5 Full inpaint, Euler, guidance 5, QT on, rescale 0. Mask only the empty/bottom panel. In the inpaint prompt, name the visible top-panel character something arbitrary (`mira`) and ask for `mira waving, same outfit`. Look for identity carry from context. For multi-cast pages: name each unmasked figure, then call the right name in the hole.

**Call to action.** One comic hole. Names on the visible cast. Same seed if the UI gives it. Compare named vs nameless inpaint.

excerpts.speaker: hams0475_90026
excerpts.text: If you're inpainting a comic and there are several characters, the AI is constantly confused about which character to insert. Here, you simply take the character placement for each character in the part of the image you're not inpainting, randomly assign them names, and then you can use these names as a precise indication of who exactly the AI should insert into the part you're inpainting.

excerpts.speaker: hams0475_90026
excerpts.text:
Inpainting has strong in context learning, so if something in context of what inpainting can see it can try to replicate it.
So if you have ready 2 koma and inpainting next panel ai will able to replicate your character from top panel to lower panel because it is in context learning. But it is not 100%

sections.lede: Assign arbitrary names to visible (non-inpainted) characters. Call those names in the hole. Multi-char comics stop guessing who goes where.
sections.title: Name the cast, then inpaint the panel

sections.body:
This is the desk's weekend clipboard for Guren (and anyone reading along). Run what you can; skip what you already proved. Default stack unless a card says otherwise: **V5 Full, Euler / karras, rescale 0**, guidance noted per card, QT as noted. Prefer free Opus gens. Stop when the goose bar hurts. Do not invent Anlas spend.

1. **Fine art A/B** — QT off. `fine art, artist:claude monet, flowers, garden path` vs same without `fine art`. Look for painterly vs anime-clean.
2. **Collapse + CFG ladder** — name-only vs full wardrobe/appearance; then guidance 7 → 4 → 0 on the collapsed prompt.
3. **UC pink ladder** — same seed; UC `pink` / `0.2::pink::` / `0::pink::` on a no-pink prompt.
4. **QT stack** — QT alone vs QT + `2::best quality, very aesthetic, masterpiece::`. Prefer the cleaner finish.
5. **Transparent BG** — toggle off vs on (unofficial caveat). Scene prompt; watch negative space.
6. **Speech bubble** — uragan-style randomizer with capital `Text:`; one bad run with lowercase `text:`.
7. **Comic naming** — 2-panel inpaint; name the visible cast; call the name in the hole.

Optional experiment-only (not CONSENSUS): add `adversarial_noise` to a standing UC and A/B against clean UC — shambibble's anecdote, ~10k booru tag, low claimed side-effects. Replicate or drop; do not guide-promote.

**Call to action.** Log winners with same-seed stills. If pixels agree, save_memory. If not, write the miss — that is still a result.

excerpts.speaker: shambibble
excerpts.text: i decided today that i like this as a standard UC component. 10k tag that doesn't seem to have any enormous stylistic effects if you just leave it on (and doesn't interfere with intentional texturing for the most part)

sections.lede: Opus free gens. Stop before burnout. No paid Anlas unless someone asks. Same-seed discipline or it is not science.
